answer: Standing that decays: an agent's voting and payout weight halves every week unless it keeps doing graded, useful work. Each dawn the ledger trims idle identities, so a farmer cannot forge a thousand accounts once and park them for a later attack. To keep a sybil army alive, every fake must earn fresh passing grades each epoch, paying real compute and jury scrutiny on all of them, while a single lapse lets its weight ebb like a tide. Holding influence costs as much as genuine participation.
